title: Mastering the Excimer Laser: Refractive Surgery Precision
summary: The Excimer laser (Excited Dimer) is the gold standard for corneal refractive surgery, utilizing 193nm ultraviolet-C light to perform precise photoablation of the corneal stroma. This platform revolutionizes visual rehabilitation by reshaping the anterior curvature with sub-micron accuracy.

sections.title: Biophysics of Photoablation
sections.content: The excimer laser (ArF - Argon Fluoride) produces photons at 193nm. Unlike thermal lasers, this is 'cold ablation'. Each pulse breaks molecular bonds (photo-decomposition) without generating significant heat, preventing thermal damage to the adjacent stroma. The process is governed by the Munnerlyn Formula: Ablation Depth = (Diameter² × Diopters) / 3.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: 193nm wavelength is absorbed by the cornea, preventing intraocular penetration.
Ablation rate is approx 0.25 microns per pulse.
Always maintain a strict corneal bed thickness (residual stromal thickness > 250-300 microns).
Active eye-tracking systems (>250Hz) are essential to compensate for saccadic movements.

content.explanation: S: Stromal bed (>250µm), T: Topography (Check for keratoconus), A: Age (>18 and stable), B: Best Corrected Visual Acuity (Exclude amblyopia).

sections.title: Ablation Mechanism Process
content: Step 1: Argon gas excitation by high voltage.
Step 2: Creation of excited dimer state.
Step 4: Molecular bond cleavage in corneal stroma.
